editorial:
Imagine spending your entire night alone in a giant, empty office building. That is exactly where you find the main character in this story. He is just a guy doing a boring job until he sees something he was never supposed to see. The whole movie feels like a slow burn that keeps you on edge. You really feel for the guy because he is just trying to get through his shift, but suddenly he is caught in a scary situation. It starts off quiet, but the tension builds up as you realize he is not as alone as he thinks he is.

What really works here is how the movie uses the empty space to make you feel uneasy. The acting is solid, and the way the story unfolds keeps you guessing about what will happen next. It might feel a bit slow for some people, but if you like thrillers that build pressure, you will love it.
endingExplained: At the end, the tension finally snaps when the man realizes the people he saw are coming for him. He tries to hide and escape the building, but the situation turns deadly. The big twist is that he cannot escape the cycle of violence. He ends up trapped and facing the consequences of what he witnessed. It wraps up with a dark realization that seeing too much can be a death sentence in a corporate world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow-burn thrillers and stories about being trapped.
